INDICATIONS AND USAGE ZEGFROVY is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 20 insertion mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test [see Dosage and Administration (2.1) ] , whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response [see Clinical Studies (14) ] . Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s). ZEGFROVY is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 20 insertion mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test, whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and effectiveness of ZEGFROVY in pediatric patients have not been established.
interactions: 7. DRUG INTERACTIONS Strong CYP3A Inhibitors : Avoid concomitant use. If concomitant use cannot be avoided, reduce ZEGFROVY dose. ( 2.4 , 7.1 ) Strong and Moderate CYP3A Inducers : Avoid concomitant use. If concomitant use cannot be avoided, increase ZEGFROVY dose. ( 2.4 , 7.1 ) P-gp or BCRP Substrates : Monitor for increased adverse reactions during concomitant use with ZEGFROVY. ( 7.2 ) Hormonal Contraceptives : Avoid concomitant use. ( 7.2 ) 7.1 Effect of Other Drugs on ZEGFROVY Table 4 describes drug interactions where coadministration with another drug affects ZEGFROVY. Table 4: Effect of Other Drugs on ZEGFROVY Strong CYP3A Inhibitors Prevention or Management Avoid concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If concomitant use cannot be avoided, reduce ZEGFROVY dose as recommended [see Dosage and Administration (2.4) ] and monitor for increased ZEGFROVY adverse reactions. Mechanism and Clinical Effect(s) Sunvozertinib is a CYP3A substrate. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases sunvozertinib exposure [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ], which may increase the risk of ZEGFROVY-associated adverse reactions. Strong or Moderate CYP3A Inducers Prevention or Management Avoid concomitant use with strong and moderate CYP3A inducers. If concomitant use cannot be avoided, increase ZEGFROVY dose as recommended [see Dosage and Administration (2.4) ]. Mechanism and Clinical Effect(s) Sunvozertinib is a CYP3A substrate. Concomitant use with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decreases sunvozertinib exposure [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ], which may reduce effectiveness of ZEGFROVY. 7.2 Effect of ZEGFROVY on Other Drugs Table 5 describes drug interactions where coadministration with ZEGFROVY affects another drug. Table 5: Effect of ZEGFROVY on Other Drugs Hormonal Contraceptives (CYP3A Substrates) Prevention or Management Avoid concomitant use of ZEGFROVY with hormonal contraceptives. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment with ZEGFROVY and for 2 weeks after the last dose. Mechanism and Clinical Effect(s) Sunvozertinib is an inducer of CYP3A4. Concomitant use of ZEGFROVY with CYP3A substrates decreased their plasma concentrations [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] , where minimal concentration changes may lead to therapeutic failure of hormonal contraceptives. P-gp or BCRP Substrates Prevention or Management Monitor for increased adverse reactions of P-gp or BCRP substrates, where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions, when coadministered with ZEGFROVY. Mechanism and Clinical Effect(s) Sunvozertinib is an inhibitor of P-gp and BCRP. ZEGFROVY increases exposure of P-gp or BCRP substrates [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ], which may increase the risk of adverse reactions associated with these substrates.
